hero.purpose: the desktop landing page headline only.

display.purpose: page titles on phones and compact views, such as "Nearby caches".

title.purpose: the name of the thing a page is about, such as a cache or place ("Krentzman Quad"). Card titles in lists use Body Strong instead.

heading.purpose: section headings in a page, such as "Hints"; also the phone wordmark and phone menu links.

wordmark.purpose: The "HuskyCache" name beside the logo in the header.

body-large.purpose: larger reading text. No component uses it yet.

body.purpose: default reading text and input text.

body-strong.purpose: emphasis in body text, card titles and the locked hint name.

action.purpose: larger button text. The Button component uses Label; no component uses Action yet.

label.purpose: button text, field labels and "Difficulty N".

small.purpose: help text, locations, metadata and "Tap to reveal".

shadows.name: pin
shadows.purpose: Map pins, and a control floating over a photo (the heart's white circle on a cache card photo).

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Popups, the map card and menus. Figma style: Shadow / Overlay; code token shadow-overlay.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The shared easing for every UI animation (the theme ease-out).

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons and hint rows shrink while pressed so a tap feels heard.

motion.name: hint-reveal
motion.purpose: A hint revealed by a tap fades in and rises; fade only with reduced motion.

motion.name: trail-draw
motion.purpose: The walked trail line draws down to the newly revealed hint; instant with reduced motion.

motion.name: pin-hover
motion.purpose: Clickable map pins only grow on hover; decorative pins stay still; skipped with reduced motion.

focusRing.purpose: Shared keyboard focus ring: 2px Focus Blue with a 2px white gap, keyboard only.

narrative.overview:
HuskyCache looks like a pocket field guide a student takes outside: calm, paper-toned pages, bold headings that name the place, and a few strong marks that say what to do next. Husky Red marks what's still out there to find, Found Green ticks off what you've found, and solid ink stars record how good it was. Everything else stays in the background so those marks read at a glance, on a phone, outdoors, in daylight.

Components are friendly and sturdy. Corners are softly rounded, borders are thin, and fills are plain. Targets are big enough to hit while walking (48px buttons, fields and hint rows; 28px stars). Type does the expressive work: Bricolage Grotesque gives headings a little character, and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next keeps everything people read and tap as legible as possible.

The look is confident but never official. HuskyCache is an unofficial student project, so it nods to campus life without borrowing a university's crests, seals or institutional layouts. It also stays away from two other directions: the dense, gradient-card look of a corporate dashboard, and the mascots, confetti and candy colors of a kids' game.
keyCharacteristics: Sage-tinted neutrals: an off-white page, white surfaces, gray-green borders, near-black ink.
Five meaning colors, each with one job: red (to find, the main action), green (found), gold (the selected map pin), pink (a favorite), blue (keyboard focus).
Gently rounded controls (8px) and cards (16px); fully round only for pins, avatars, pill tags, icon buttons (the heart) and the header's search and pages.
Flat surfaces; only things that float above the page cast a shadow: map pins, the heart's white circle on a photo, and overlays (popups, the map card, menus, the login dialog).
Bricolage Grotesque headings, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything else, JetBrains Mono only for secret codes.
Mobile-first, built for one-handed, outdoor use; desktop is the same system with more room.

rules.name: The Bright Sun Rule
rules.body: Anything that carries meaning must stay readable with Increase Contrast on. Anything that's only mood is allowed to vanish.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Red, green, gold, pink and blue each mean exactly one thing. Never use them for decoration, for headings, or to make something "pop".

rules.name: The One Red Button Rule
rules.body: A page has at most one Husky Red button. Every other action is Secondary.

rules.name: The Links Go Places Rule
rules.body: A link takes you to another page and sits inside a sentence ("…on the cache's edit page."). Anything that does something (saves, prints, copies, adds, starts over) is a button, and so is anything standing on its own line. Actions step down in weight: Primary (one per page), then Secondary, then a quiet button with no outline for anything lesser. A page full of underlined links reads as clutter, so when one stands alone, make it a button.

rules.name: The Tokens Only Rule
rules.body: Use the token classes (`bg-accent`, `text-text-secondary`), never raw hex values.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Bricolage for headings and the brand, Atkinson for everything people read and tap, JetBrains Mono only for secret codes. Never a fourth face.

rules.name: The 16px Floor Rule
rules.body: Text people type is at least 16px, so phones don't zoom in.

rules.name: The Text Style Rule
rules.body: Each text style class sets the font, size, line height, weight and tracking together. Use the class (`text-title`), not raw pixel sizes.

rules.name: The Flat Field Rule
rules.body: Cards, buttons and fields never cast shadows. If something needs to stand out, give it a border or a fill. The one exception is a control floating over a photo, which has no page under it to stand out from: it takes the Pin shadow.

dos: **Do** keep each meaning color to its one job: Husky Red for to-find and the main action, Found Green for found, Pin Gold for the selected pin, Favorite Pink for favorited hearts, Focus Blue for keyboard focus.
**Do** show difficulty as bars plus "Difficulty N", and ratings as stars, so the two are never confused.
**Do** pair every color signal with a shape or words: a check for found, a label for difficulty, an icon and message for errors.
**Do** keep tap targets at least 28px, and buttons, fields and hint rows at 48px.
**Do** use the shared focus ring (2px Focus Blue, 2px gap) on everything focusable.
**Do** follow The Bright Sun Rule (see Colors → Increase Contrast).
**Do** use the theme tokens and text style classes instead of raw values.

**Do** keep motion for changes someone caused (a reveal, a press), on the shared ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, the theme's `ease-out`), and respect reduced motion. Each animation stays under 300ms; a follow-up sequenced after the first change (like the trail drawing after a hint appears) may start up to 100ms later, so a sequence can total about 350ms.
donts: **Don't** make it look like an official Northeastern site: no crests, seals, official-looking university layouts, or anything implying university approval.
**Don't** make it look like a corporate dashboard: no dense data panels, gradient cards or enterprise styling.
**Don't** make it look like a kids' game: no cartoon mascots, confetti bursts or candy colors.
**Don't** put more than one Husky Red button on a page.

**Don't** add shadows to cards, buttons or fields; shadows are only for map pins and floating overlays (popups, the map card, menus, the login dialog), plus the Pin shadow on a control floating over a photo (The Flat Field Rule).
**Don't** use Pin Gold for text, or for anything but the selected pin.
**Don't** add a fourth typeface, or use JetBrains Mono for anything but secret codes.
**Don't** put information in the contour backdrop or use it as a fill; it's mood, and it disappears with Increase Contrast.

**Don't** animate decoration (such as the contour rings), stagger page entrances, smooth-scroll when focus moves, or give a hover effect to something that can't be clicked. Save celebrations for the moment they happen ("Find logged!" and "Cache hidden!"), not for states seen later, like "Found by you".
